mainTopic: How each disqualified animal in the משנה could first be fit, why the משנה lists three 'not yet fit' cases, and the source for רבי שמעון's לאו on a מחוסר זמן.
overview: The גמרא wants every case in the משנה to be an animal that was fit at first for the פתח אהל מועד and only later became disqualified. For רובע and נרבע this is easy: the animal was made holy first, and the act happened afterward. מוקצה and נעבד happen only with קדשים קלים, which רבי יוסי הגלילי holds are still the owner's property, and a ברייתא proves he holds this. אתנן, מחיר, כלאים and יוצא דופן are about the babies of holy animals, because the תנא holds such babies become holy only at birth. Next the גמרא explains why the משנה needs all three cases of the argument between רבי שמעון and the חכמים: temporarily blemished animals, doves whose time has not come, and אותו ואת בנו. Then it finds the source for רבי שמעון's לאו in 'לא תעשון'. In גלגל, obligatory offerings were like a מחוסר זמן compared to שילה, and משה forbade them. At the end, רבי ירמיה begins a challenge to this source, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Bestiality cases work, but how can idol-worship cases happen after consecration?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that רובע and נרבע can happen after the animal was made קדוש. It then challenges how מוקצה and נעבד could ever happen to a קרבן, since a person cannot make forbidden what is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for an animal involved in bestiality, you can find a case where it was made holy first and only afterward was involved in bestiality. But an animal set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped: a person cannot make forbidden something that does not belong to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first agrees that the bestiality cases are easy to explain. Then it raises a challenge: the idol-worship cases seem impossible to explain the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is to find each animal fit at first and only disqualified later. Bestiality can happen to any animal, even one already made קדוש. Making an animal מוקצה or נעבד works by the owner's own act, though, and once the animal is הקדש it is no longer his, so he should not be able to make it forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (opens the part that is fine, before the problem)
An animal that actively had relations with a person / an animal that was used for bestiality
An animal set aside for idol worship / an animal that was itself worshipped

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person cannot make forbidden something that does not belong to him
At first / from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying מוקצה and נעבד are not real disqualifications. The only question is how they could happen to an animal that is already הקדש.

phrases.english: Granted, an animal that had relations with a person, or was used for bestiality:
you can find it where he consecrated them at first,
and afterward they were involved in bestiality.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא but the corrected text leaves it out; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: But an animal set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ!
phrases.english: a person cannot make forbidden something that is not his!
phrases.notes: Once the animal is consecrated it belongs to הקדש, not to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of why the משנה needs a פסוק to exempt these animals, by trying to show each one was once fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that every case in the משנה can be an animal that was first consecrated and only later disqualified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מוקצה and נעבד need the owner's act. After consecration the animal is not his, and a person cannot forbid what is not his, so these cases can't happen after consecration.

steps.title: The case is קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the idol-worship cases happen with קדשים קלים, which רבי יוסי הגלילי considers the owner's property, so he can make them forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about offerings of lesser holiness, and it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says that offerings of lesser holiness are the owner's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case to קדשים קלים, following the opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a קרבן is not the owner's, so he can't forbid it. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that קדשים קלים, such as a שלמים, still count as the owner's money. So the owner can make them מוקצה or נעבד even after he consecrated them.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness (such as שלמים)
According to the opinion of
The owner's property

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the משנה's list of מוקצה and נעבד fits the 'fit at first, disqualified later' model only for קדשים קלים, and only according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: It is with offerings of lesser sanctity,
and according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים הוּא.
phrases.english: who says: offerings of lesser sanctity are the owner's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific type of קרבן and a specific opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every קרבן belongs to הקדש, so no owner could make it forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: With קדשים קלים, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the animal is still the owner's, so he can make it מוקצה or נעבד after consecrating it.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי treats קדשים קלים as the owner's money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'ומעלה מעל בה׳' that a false oath about a friend's קדשים קלים counts, because they are the friend's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'and commits a trespass against ה׳': this comes to include offerings of lesser holiness, since they are his property. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי יוסי הגלילי really holds the view it just quoted, by bringing a ברייתא with his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about someone who falsely denies holding his friend's property. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it also covers denying a friend's קדשים קלים. That only makes sense if קדשים קלים still count as the friend's own money.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And commits a trespass against ה׳‎' (ויקרא 5:21)
To include

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And commits a trespass against the Lord":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21, about someone who falsely swears he isn't holding his friend's property.

phrases.english: to include offerings of lesser sanctity, since they are his property.
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion of רבי יוסי הגלילי used in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds קדשים קלים are the owner's property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'ומעלה מעל בה׳' (ויקרא 5:21) to include a false oath about another's קדשים קלים.

steps.title: Summary: how each case in the משנה happens after consecration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: רובע and נרבע happen after consecration through an act of ערוה, and מוקצה and נעבד happen after consecration through עבודה זרה, in קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: an animal involved in bestiality is disqualified through a forbidden act of relations. An animal set aside or worshipped is disqualified through idol worship, in offerings of lesser holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its summary (הלכך) of how each case in the משנה can be an animal that was fit at first and disqualified only later. This step covers רובע, נרבע, מוקצה and נעבד, and the next step continues the same summary with אתנן, מחיר, כלאים and יוצא דופן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bestiality cases work with any קרבן, because they don't depend on ownership. The idol-worship cases work only with קדשים קלים, because they depend on the owner having the power to forbid the animal. So all four animals were once fit for the פתח אהל מועד, which is why a פסוק is needed to exempt them.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
A matter of forbidden relations
Idol worship

steps.whatToRemember: Every case in the משנה can be an animal that was first fit and only later disqualified. רובע and נרבע work with any קרבן. מוקצה and נעבד work only with קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי, because the owner can forbid only what is his.

phrases.english: Therefore, an animal involved in bestiality: it is a matter of forbidden relations.
Set aside or worshipped: it is idol worship,
in offerings of lesser sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the answer from steps 2 and 3 into one summary of all four cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רובע and נרבע are disqualified after consecration through ערוה with any קרבן. מוקצה and נעבד are disqualified after consecration through עבודה זרה only in קדשים קלים, which are the owner's property according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: Payment, price, mixed breed and C-section cases are about babies of holy animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that אתנן, מחיר, כלאים and יוצא דופן can strike a קרבן because the משנה is talking about the offspring of holy animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal given as payment to a prostitute (אתנן), an animal given as the price of a dog (מחיר), a mixed-breed animal (כלאים), and an animal born by C-section (יוצא דופן): these cases are about the babies of holy animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues answering the earlier question of how each problem in the משנה can happen after the animal is already holy. For these four problems, the answer is that we are talking about the babies of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four problems seem impossible for a holy animal: you can't pay a prostitute with a קרבן, and a mixed breed or C-section animal is unfit from the start. The answer is that the animal came from a holy mother, so it belonged to the world of קדשים before the problem took hold. Only at or after birth does it end up unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal given as payment to a prostitute; it may not be brought as a קרבן
An animal received in exchange for a dog; it may not be brought as a קרבן
An animal born from two different species
An animal born by C-section, through the side wall of the mother
The babies born to animals that are holy as קרבנות

phrases.english: Payment to a prostitute, and the price of a dog,
a mixed breed, an animal born by C-section –
these are about the offspring of holy animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶתְנַן, וּמְחִיר, כִּלְאַיִם, יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן – בִּוְלָדוֹת קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 1-4 covered how רובע, נרבע, מוקצה and נעבד happen after consecration. This step covers the remaining items in the same way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה refers to the babies of holy animals
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These four problems could never happen to an animal that was already holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: They happen to the offspring of holy animals, which can still become unfit.

steps.title: Babies of holy animals become holy only at birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the view behind the answer: the תנא holds that the babies of holy animals become holy as they come into being, at birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of the משנה holds that the babies of holy animals become holy only when they come into being, at birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning that makes the last answer work. It tells us what this תנא holds about when a holy animal's baby becomes holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a baby inside a holy mother is already holy, so a status like אתנן could not take effect on it. This תנא holds that the baby's holiness starts only at birth. So while it is still inside the mother, the baby can still pick up a problem like אתנן, and then it is born holy but unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (introduces the view or reasoning behind a ruling)
At the time they come into being, at birth
The offspring of holy animals

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the mother and the baby. The mother is already holy, but according to this תנא the baby's own holiness only begins at birth. That gap is what allows the problem to take hold.

phrases.english: He holds: the offspring of holy animals –
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of our משנה.

phrases.english: they become holy as they come into being.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים – בַּהֲוָיָיתָן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the underlying view that makes Step 5's answer work.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the underlying view of the תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A baby inside a holy mother is already holy, so אתנן or מחיר could not take effect on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא holds the baby becomes holy only at birth, so the problem can take effect first.
steps.whatToRemember: All the problems in this part of the משנה can strike after consecration. רובע and נרבע happen through an act of ערוה, מוקצה and נעבד happen through עבודה זרה in קדשים קלים, and אתנן, מחיר, כלאים and יוצא דופן happen with the babies of holy animals, which become holy only at birth.

steps.title: Quoting the next part of the משנה: temporary blemishes and אותו ואת בנו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next section of the משנה, where רבי שמעון and the חכמים argue about animals that are only temporarily unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: animals with a passing blemish, and so on; an animal and its baby slaughtered on the same day, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next lines of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון says one who offers these 'not yet fit' animals outside the עזרה breaks a לאו. The חכמים say he is פטור. The cases are an animal with a temporary blemish, doves whose time has not come, and the second animal of אותו ואת בנו slaughtered on the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a blemish; here, a blemish that will pass
The ban on slaughtering an animal and its baby on the same day
Etc.; the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: Blemished animals, etc.,
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about a blemish that will go away, so the animal will become fit later.

phrases.english: It and its offspring, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין וְכוּ׳, אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the list of disqualifications to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון holds there is a לאו for offering 'not yet fit' animals outside. The חכמים say he is פטור.

steps.title: Why all three cases are needed: blemished animals versus young doves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכותא. If only blemished animals were taught, we might think the חכמים exempt there only because such animals are repulsive, but agree with רבי שמעון about young doves.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the cases are needed. If the משנה had taught only blemished animals, we would say the חכמים exempt there because blemished animals are repulsive. But with doves, which are not repulsive, I would say the חכמים do not exempt, and they agree with רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to list more than one example of the same argument. It starts by showing that the blemished-animal case alone would not teach us about the doves. Steps 9 and 10 finish the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים exempt someone who offers a 'not yet fit' animal outside. With a blemished animal, we might think the reason is that a blemished animal is disgusting as a קרבן, so it is not seen as a real offering. Young doves are not disgusting, so without the משנה spelling it out we might think the חכמים agree they count.

keyTerms.meaning: And they are needed; opens a צריכותא explaining why each case must be taught
They are repulsive or disgusting
Doves (turtledoves) brought as קרבנות
I would say

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אימא לא' is not the conclusion. It is what we would have wrongly thought if the משנה had taught only one case. This is exactly why the משנה lists the doves too.

phrases.english: And they are all needed;
for if it had taught only blemished animals –
the חכמים exempt because they are repulsive;
but doves, which are not repulsive –
phrases.notes: These are doves too young to be brought yet. They are part of the 'etc.' in the משנה quote.

phrases.english: I would say no,
that they agree with רבי שמעון;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה quoted in Step 7 needed to list several cases of the same argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blemished-animal case alone would not teach the doves case, because the חכמים' reason might be that blemished animals are repulsive.
steps.whyThisMatters: A צריכותא shows that no case in the משנה is extra. Each one rules out a different wrong guess about the reason behind the חכמים' view.

steps.title: Second leg: why the case of young doves is not enough
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only תורין, we might think רבי שמעון forbids them only because they were never fit, but agrees with the חכמים about blemished animals, which were fit and then pushed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only doves, I would say רבי שמעון holds there is a prohibition because they were never fit and then pushed off. But blemished animals were fit and then pushed off, so I would say no: רבי שמעון agrees with the חכמים there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its explanation of why the משנה lists more than one case. Now it shows why teaching only the case of young doves would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Young doves were never fit yet; they are simply waiting for their time. Blemished animals were once fit and then became unfit. We might have thought that being pushed off makes a bigger difference, so רבי שמעון would agree they carry no prohibition. Teaching the blemished case shows he does not agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves. Here it means doves that are not yet old enough to be brought as a קרבן.
They were fit and then were pushed off (became unfit).
Agrees, concedes.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only doves,
that would be because they were never fit and then pushed off;
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: but blemished animals,
which were fit and then pushed off,
I would say: no,
that Rabbi Shimon agrees with the Rabbis about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second part of the צריכותא started in step 8, this time looking at the opposite direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching only doves would leave room to think that רבי שמעון agrees with the חכמים about temporarily blemished animals.

steps.title: Third leg: why אותו ואת בנו is also needed, so all three cases are necessary
steps.stepSummary: If only the first two cases were taught, we might think the חכמים exempt there because the flaw is in the animal itself, but agree with רבי שמעון about אותו ואת בנו, where the flaw comes from outside. So all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only these two cases, I would say the חכמים exempt there because the flaw is in the animals themselves. But in אותו ואת בנו the flaw comes from outside, so I would say the חכמים agree with רבי שמעון. Therefore all are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last part of the צריכותא, explaining why the משנה also needed the case of אותו ואת בנו. It then concludes that every case is necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemish or being too young is a flaw in the animal's own body. In אותו ואת בנו the young animal is perfectly fine; the only problem is that its parent was slaughtered that same day. We might have thought the חכמים would agree with רבי שמעון in that case, so the משנה had to show that they disagree here too.

keyTerms.meaning: A flaw in their own body, coming from the animal itself.
An animal and its child, which may not be slaughtered on the same day.
A flaw that comes from outside the animal.
It is necessary: each case teaches something the others could not.

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three cases teaches something new: young doves were never fit, blemished animals were fit and then pushed off, and אותו ואת בנו has a flaw from outside. The argument applies to all three.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only these two,
phrases.notes: These two are the blemished animals and the young doves.

phrases.english: I would say that is because the flaw is in their own bodies;
but an animal and its child,
where the flaw comes to it from outside,
phrases.notes: The young animal itself is fine. The problem is only that its parent was slaughtered that day.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: I would say the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Shimon;
therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא from steps 8 and 9 and closes it with צריכא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה needed all three cases, because each one alone could have been read as a place where one side agrees with the other.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי שמעון's prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words from the משנה and asks what his reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "For רבי שמעון used to say..." What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the words of רבי שמעון. It asks where his prohibition comes from, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says that someone who brings such a קרבן outside the עזרה breaks a prohibition, but there is no כרת. He does not say which prohibition, so the גמרא wants to know the source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Often it asks for the source of a ruling.
For he used to say. These are the opening words being quoted from the משנה.

phrases.english: The משנה said: "For Rabbi Shimon used to say":
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the צריכותא, the גמרא opens a new topic: the source for רבי שמעון's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק or reason behind רבי שמעון's prohibition against bringing outside the עזרה an animal that will only become fit later.

steps.title: ריש לקיש brings a פסוק: voluntary offerings yes, obligatory offerings no
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא, quoting ריש לקיש, brings the פסוק "לא תעשון ככל אשר אנחנו עשים פה היום." In it משה told the people that when they enter the land they may bring voluntary offerings but not obligatory ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of ריש לקיש: The פסוק says, "You shall not do all that we do here this day." משה told the Jewish people: When you enter the land, you may bring voluntary offerings, but you may not bring obligatory offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. ריש לקיש explains it as משה telling the people which קרבנות they may bring when they first enter ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after entering the land, the people could bring offerings they chose to give (ישרות), but obligatory offerings (חובות) had to wait for a later time. So the תורה here speaks about a קרבן whose time has not yet come. This is the kind of case רבי שמעון is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, a verse.
You shall not do. These are the words of the prohibition.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון's prohibition comes from "לא תעשון ככל אשר אנחנו עשים פה היום," which ריש לקיש reads as allowing voluntary offerings but forbidding obligatory ones when the people first enter the land.

steps.title: Gilgal offerings counted as not yet in their time
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's answer is completed. Obligatory offerings in the time of גלגל were like a מחוסר זמן compared to שילה, and משה forbade them with 'לא תעשון.' So bringing a מחוסר זמן is a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And גלגל, compared to שילה, is a case of 'not yet in its time.' Yet משה told them: 'You shall not do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how the פסוק from step 12 proves רבי שמעון's view. The obligatory offerings that had to wait for שילה were 'not yet in their time' while the people were in גלגל, and משה used the words 'לא תעשון' for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed that משה allowed only voluntary offerings until the people were settled. Here the גמרא adds the missing link. Since obligatory offerings were only waiting for their proper time, they were like a מחוסר זמן. Because the פסוק says 'לא תעשון' about them, offering a מחוסר זמן carries a לאו, just as רבי שמעון said.

keyTerms.meaning: The first place the משכן stood after the people entered the land

An offering whose time has not yet come
'You shall not do,' the wording that makes this a לאו

steps.whatToRemember: The source for רבי שמעון's לאו: obligatory offerings in גלגל were like a מחוסר זמן, and משה said 'לא תעשון' about them.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two places. In גלגל only voluntary offerings could be brought. The obligatory ones had to wait for שילה, so in גלגל they were 'not yet in their time.'

steps.title: רבי ירמיה begins to challenge the derivation
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says to רבי זירא, 'If so,' and opens a challenge to the source just given.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: If that is so...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבי ירמיה starts a challenge with 'אי הכי,' but the actual difficulty comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אי הכי' means 'if what you just said is true.' It signals that the source from step 13 is about to be pushed further, to show it leads to a result that seems too broad. So far only the opening of the challenge appears.
